recipes.title: Audio briefing production

description.need: An approved script is not a listenable briefing, and hand editing every segment into one track is the step that stops briefings from shipping regularly.
description.input: An approved multi segment script with host turns, a target runtime, and any pacing or intro material the adopter supplies.
description.core_action: Synthesize each segment as speech, join the segments into one coherent track with deliberate pacing between them, and judge the result against the runtime the script promised before calling it finished.
description.output: A single finished audio file whose pacing and length were verified, ready for a listen and a final decision rather than for further editing.

activities.label: Read the approved script and its segment structure
Settle voice pairing and pacing against what has been approved before
Synthesize each segment as speech
Join segments into one track with the intended spacing
Check the finished track against the promised runtime
Hand over the finished file for a listen

outcomes.statement: An approved script becomes a listenable, correctly paced final audio file without manual editing.
success_criteria: Segment audio joins with natural pacing, verified by a duration check rather than by a successful render
The delivered file is ready for review, not a rough cut

recipes.guidance: Turn an approved script into a finished audio file: synthesize each segment, join it into one coherent track, and verify the result actually sounds and runs right before calling it done. Learn from what gets approved; voice, pacing and hook preferences from approvals are worth remembering. Treat a failed duration check as a real defect rather than a formality, and when one segment fails, keep the rest and say which one is missing.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The work has one honest starting point, a person approving a script. Nothing here is worth doing on a clock, and nothing can be done before the approval exists.

personalization_needs: Which voices belong to which host role for this adopter, because the pairing is a taste decision the recipe cannot guess and it carries across every future briefing
How long a briefing should actually run and how much pacing silence the adopter wants between turns, since the duration check is meaningless without a target they chose
Whether a finished file should be delivered as a file, into a folder, or into a publishing queue, because that decides what done means

input_schema.name: segment_silence_ms
input_schema.description: Silence inserted between segments for pacing.

input_schema.name: intro_music_path
input_schema.description: Optional intro audio concatenated before the briefing.

examples.title: ElevenLabs as the speech connector
examples.notes: Catalogued as ai plus voice_generation. Per segment synthesis with a stable voice id is what makes the host pairing reproducible across briefings; a changed voice id silently changes the show.

examples.title: Deepgram as the speech connector
examples.notes: Catalogued as ai, transcription and voice_generation. Chosen when the same installation already uses it for transcription; the transcription half is unused by this recipe.

recipes.review_notes: v2 listed connectors as voice_generation plus desktop. desktop is dropped by the v3 rule; voice_generation was already a catalog category and stays. The ffmpeg dependency is genuinely evidenced by the v2 error handling (FFmpeg missing produces an install instruction), so it is the one real dependency in this half of the lane. The v2 trigger was an internal event on briefing.script_approved; kept as event because the underlying fact is a human approval, not an internal pipeline hand off. The 300ms silence and the 25 percent duration tolerance stayed in input_schema and guidance respectively rather than in the description, since they are knobs and not the craft.
recipes.research_notes: Read scripts/connectors/builtin/elevenlabs.json and deepgram.json. elevenlabs categories are ai and voice_generation; deepgram categories are ai, transcription and voice_generation, so a single voice_generation type resolves to both plus huggingface. No connector in the catalog performs audio concatenation, which is why ffmpeg is a dependency and not a connector_type.

recipes.title: Audio briefing script drafting

description.need: Source material read aloud verbatim does not hold a listener, and discovering that after paying for synthesis is the expensive way to find out.
description.input: One piece of source material in whatever form it arrived, pasted text, a file, a fetched page, or another agent's output, plus the adopter's intent for what to emphasise.
description.core_action: Find the headline finding, the facts that carry it, the tensions worth airing and the questions left open, then shape them into two host turns that pace correctly when spoken rather than when read.
description.output: A structured script with a named host cast and turn by turn segments, held for a human decision before anything is synthesized.

activities.label: Read the source material through
Settle the headline finding, key facts, tensions and open questions
Choose the host pairing that fits the material
Write turn by turn segments paced for speech
Present the outline, script and cast for a decision

outcomes.statement: Any source material becomes a structured, pacing aware two host script that survives human review before it costs anything to produce.
success_criteria: The script captures headline finding, key facts, tensions and open questions from the source, not just a paraphrase
Nothing goes to audio synthesis without human approval first

recipes.guidance: Distil whatever source material comes in into a two host script that actually holds together: a real headline, the facts that matter, the tensions worth exploring, and turns that pace well when spoken aloud. This is a drafting job, not a summarising one; the structure and pacing decisions are the value. Hold for approval before anything moves to paid synthesis, and when the same draft is turned down three times, the style is wrong rather than the attempt.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Sources arrive when the adopter has something worth briefing on. There is no external event and no calendar obligation; the persona works down what is waiting and stops when nothing is.

personalization_needs: What the adopter wants emphasised and what downplayed, in their own words, because the same source yields opposite scripts for a technical audience and an executive one
Who is listening, since host roles, vocabulary and how much context to restate all follow from the audience rather than from the source
How long a briefing should run, because pacing decisions are made against a target and a script written without one is untestable

input_schema.name: briefing_style
input_schema.description: Picks host roles: casual (curious explainer + sharp questioner), formal (domain expert + skeptical reviewer), news (anchor + reporter), executive (strategic summarizer + operational realist).

input_schema.name: target_duration_minutes
input_schema.description: Target runtime. Script auto-shrinks if it exceeds target by >20%.

input_schema.name: briefing_intent
input_schema.description: Free-text hints: what to emphasize, what to downplay, tone adjustments, audience. The persona reads this each run.

recipes.review_notes: v2 declared no connectors and that survives review: a source arrives as pasted text or a file in most runs, and the URL case degrades to asking for a paste rather than failing, so no connector type is load bearing. Trigger moved from manual to self_paced, which is the closest of the three v3 kinds to on demand work: the persona acts on sources that are waiting. The v2 pairing with Audio Production is preserved only through the approval event on the production side; this recipe stops at a reviewed script and claims nothing about synthesis.
recipes.research_notes: No connector research was needed. Checked that no catalog category covers generic URL fetching in a way this recipe depends on: web_scraping exists (apify, bright-data, firecrawl) but the v2 source evidences a paste fallback rather than a scraping requirement, so adding it would be inventing a dependency.

recipes.title: Original 2D art generation and curation

description.need: A generated art library grows into noise unless somebody decides what stays, and an agent that never learns from those decisions keeps producing the same rejected work.
description.input: The subject matter and mood the curator wants explored, the history of what has already been made, and the reasons past work was turned down.
description.core_action: Conceive a direction that has not been tried, generate work in it, and present each piece for an explicit keep or discard decision rather than assuming taste.
description.output: A growing body of kept work, each piece recorded with what produced it, and a set of directions the curator has ruled out.

activities.label: Read what has already been made and what was turned down
Settle on a direction that is not a restatement
Generate the work
Present each piece for a keep or discard decision
Record what produced a kept piece and why one was discarded

outcomes.statement: There is a growing body of generated work that the person curating it actually wanted, and its direction moves with their taste.
success_criteria: Every piece is presented for an explicit keep or discard decision before it is kept
Discarded work leaves a reason behind, and repeated reasons stop showing up in later work
New pieces are not restatements of pieces already made

recipes.guidance: Conceive and generate work, then let the curator decide. The accountability is the direction over time, not any single image: a run that produces one piece worth keeping beats four near duplicates. Learn from what is turned down, especially when the reason repeats, and stop generating in that direction. Keep the record of what a kept piece was made from, because that is what makes the next one better.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when there is a direction worth exploring that has not been tried, and pause when recent work is going unreviewed, since generating into a full review queue helps nobody. The v2 daily schedule was a delivery habit, not an obligation.

personalization_needs: The subject matter and mood the adopter wants explored, in their own words rather than from a menu, because a picked style label produces work that belongs to nobody
How much say the adopter wants over each piece, because that decides whether this is a curated feed or a supervised commission
Where kept work should live, since a gallery and a project folder imply different handling and different formats

input_schema.name: art_subject
input_schema.description: Free-text description of subject matter, themes, and mood. Examples: 'fantasy landscapes with magical creatures', 'abstract geometric art inspired by architecture'.

input_schema.name: art_style
input_schema.description: Visual style for generated artwork. Refined over time from feedback.

input_schema.name: color_mood
input_schema.description: Color mood guidance for the palette.

input_schema.name: dimensions
input_schema.description: Image width by height. Larger sizes cost more credits.

input_schema.name: variations_per_run
input_schema.description: Variations generated per cycle; best one is filed.

input_schema.name: concept_history_depth
input_schema.description: How many past concepts to dedup against.

examples.title: Higgsfield as the image connector
examples.notes: Catalogued as ai, image_generation and video_generation. Same shape as Leonardo for this recipe; the choice is a credit and style decision at adoption.

recipes.title: On brand visual asset production

description.need: Surfaces ship with placeholder or stock visuals because making something that belongs to this specific product is slower than shipping without it.
description.input: The written design brief, the surface that needs art and what it is for, and the accumulated record of which phrasings produced approved work and which were turned down.
description.core_action: Compose the work from the brief rather than from scratch, judge it against the brief before showing it to anyone, and iterate a small fixed number of times rather than indefinitely.
description.output: An asset that traces to the brief, in the format and size the surface needs, delivered where the project can actually use it, after a person has seen it.

activities.label: Read the brief and the surface the asset is for
Compose the request from the brief and what has been approved before
Generate the asset
Judge the result against the brief and iterate a bounded number of times
Deliver to the surface in the format it needs, for a human decision

outcomes.statement: Surfaces that would otherwise ship with placeholder or generic visuals get work that belongs to this product.
success_criteria: Every delivered asset traces to the brief, and where it departs from it the departure is deliberate and stated
Assets land where the project can actually use them, in the format and size that surface needs
Nothing is delivered without a human seeing it first

recipes.guidance: Make the visual work the project needs and put it where the project can use it. Look for the surfaces that are still generic rather than waiting to be asked, and be honest when a surface does not need art. Judge your own output against the brief before showing it, and iterate a small number of times rather than indefinitely. When the work cannot reach the bar, ask for a reference instead of trying again.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Watch for surfaces still carrying placeholder or stock visuals, new surfaces added without art, and requests waiting. Act on request immediately and on the seat's own initiative when the queue is clear.

personalization_needs: Which project surfaces are in scope, because an unbounded remit here produces work nobody asked for
What kinds of asset the adopter needs most, which shapes what the seat gets good at over time
How assets should reach the project, since a file in a folder and a committed change are different levels of trust

input_schema.name: asset_request
input_schema.description: What to create: hero image, social media card, icon set, UI illustration, background. Include dimensions / aspect ratio if specific.

input_schema.name: asset_type
input_schema.description: Shapes memory lookup and per-type prompt templates.

input_schema.name: quality_threshold
input_schema.description: Minimum multimodal AI score before the asset proceeds to human review. Higher = more auto-iteration cycles.

recipes.title: Product design brief authoring

description.need: Without one written description of how a product should look, every piece of visual work is judged against a different unstated standard and none of it composes.
description.input: Whatever the adopter already has, an existing brief they wrote, the product's own code and surfaces, or nothing but the product itself.
description.core_action: Name concrete colour roles, type treatment and layout direction rather than adjectives, taking the adopter's own brief verbatim where one exists and doing the extraction work only where one does not.
description.output: One written brief, specific enough that two people would produce compatible work from it, reviewed by a human before anything is made from it.

activities.label: Establish where the brand direction can actually be read from
Decide whether the adopter's own brief stands as written
Write or complete the brief in concrete terms
Put the brief in front of a person before anything is made from it

outcomes.statement: There is one written description of how this product should look, specific enough that two people would produce compatible work from it.
success_criteria: The brief names concrete colour roles, type treatment and layout direction rather than adjectives like premium or modern
It matches what the product's own code and surfaces actually do, or says explicitly where it is aspirational
It is reviewed by a human before anything is made from it

recipes.guidance: Own the written brand direction that everything else is judged against. Derive it from what the product actually looks like where that exists, and accept the adopter's own brief verbatim when they have one rather than rewriting it. The failure mode is vagueness: a brief that cannot rule anything out is not a brief. Revise it when the product's real design drifts away from it, and never revise it silently.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when the product's own design has moved away from what the brief says, or when work keeps being rejected on the same brief dimension, which means the brief is wrong rather than the work.

personalization_needs: Whether the adopter already has a brief to use as is, because rewriting someone's existing brand direction is a loss and the recipe's default is to extract
Which product or surface the brief governs, since one adopter may run several with different looks
What the product should feel like to its users, which cannot be read out of code and is the half extraction always misses

input_schema.name: brief_source_intent
input_schema.description: Where the brief should be extracted from: a local file or folder path, a registered codebase, or a pasted-in design.md.

input_schema.name: brief_mode
input_schema.description: How Step 0 runs at build time. Auto-extract reads the source above; user-pasted accepts a brief verbatim; on-demand defers.

input_schema.name: brief_content
input_schema.description: The user's own design.md / brand brief pasted verbatim (from Stitch, Figma, Gemini, or hand-written). Used as-is when brief_mode is 'I'll paste my own design.md'; ignored otherwise.

examples.title: The registered local codebase as the extraction source
examples.notes: Catalogued as development, source_control and desktop. Theme files and stylesheets are what make the extraction concrete; when the project has none, the recipe falls back to asking the adopter rather than inventing colour roles.

recipes.review_notes: Outcomes, guidance and trigger from the superseding Artist responsibility. The v2 recipe hardcoded a five section structure (empathy, sensory aesthetic, four role colour hierarchy, typography hierarchy, layout metaphor); the designed responsibility does not, and states the test differently and better, that the brief must be able to rule something out. I followed the designed responsibility and dropped the five section list from the outcome, keeping the concrete colour role and type treatment requirement it names. The v2 'runs once at build time' framing is gone: the designed trigger makes revision the normal case rather than the exception.
recipes.research_notes: Checked whether a design category would be a better fit than development: design exists in the catalog (figma, canva, penpot) but the v2 recipe and the designed responsibility both read the brief out of the product's own code, not out of a design tool, so declaring design would promise a capability neither source evidences. Left at development and noted the option.

recipes.title: Feature walkthrough capture from the running app

description.need: A feature nobody can watch has to be explained by hand every time, and a walkthrough recorded from a guessed script shows screens the app does not produce.
description.input: The implementation of the feature to be shown, a running instance of the app, and whatever capture tooling exists on the machine.
description.core_action: Read the code first so the walkthrough follows the path a real user takes, then drive that path live and pace the capture for a viewer rather than for the machine.
description.output: A walkthrough artifact recorded against a known build, with any limitation of the available capture method stated in it rather than hidden.

activities.label: Read the implementation to establish the real user path
Establish what capture the machine can actually do
Plan the walkthrough steps and their pacing
Drive the path in the running app and capture it
Deliver the artifact with its build and its stated limitations

outcomes.statement: Any feature worth showing has a current walkthrough that matches what the app does today.
success_criteria: Each walkthrough records the build or commit it was captured against
A walkthrough whose screens no longer match the app is marked stale rather than served as current
A capture that failed produces a stated reason, never a silently empty file

outcomes.statement: The walkthrough follows the path a real user takes, grounded in the code that implements it.
success_criteria: The steps shown correspond to the implemented flow rather than a guessed one
A limitation of the capture method available on the machine is stated in the artifact rather than hidden

recipes.guidance: Own whether someone can watch the result and understand the feature. Read the implementation first so the walkthrough follows the real path rather than a guessed one, and pace the capture for a viewer rather than for the machine. When the capture method available on this machine cannot do what the walkthrough needs, deliver the lesser artifact with the limitation named instead of a broken one.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when a feature has shipped without a walkthrough, when the screens in an existing one no longer match the app, or when the operator asks. A stale set is worked down over time rather than recaptured wholesale.

personalization_needs: Which app and which of its surfaces are worth recording, because recording everything produces a library nobody watches
Who the walkthrough is for, since an internal review capture, an operator memory aid and a public demo differ in pacing, annotation and whether commentary is needed at all
What capture tooling actually exists on this machine, because the artifact ceiling is set by the machine and the adopter should not be promised video where only screenshots are possible
dependencies: a running local instance of the app being demonstrated
playwright (optional; unlocks the video capture tier where it is present)

input_schema.description: What feature or workflow to demo. Freeform description the recorder uses to guide codebase analysis and walkthrough planning.

input_schema.name: recording_mode
input_schema.description: Capture method. Auto-detect picks the best available tier on your system.

input_schema.name: walkthrough_speed
input_schema.description: Pacing of interactions. Slower produces clearer captures but takes longer.

input_schema.name: viewport_width
input_schema.description: Browser viewport width in pixels.

input_schema.name: viewport_height
input_schema.description: Browser viewport height in pixels.

recipes.title: Feature announcement video production

description.need: Shipped features go unannounced because a short video costs a script, a voice and a render, and getting any one of them wrong late means redoing all three.
description.input: A description of the feature, who it benefits, and the accumulated record of which tone, style and pacing the adopter has approved before.
description.core_action: Settle the script and visual strategy and get them approved before anything is synthesized or rendered, then keep rework scoped to the stage that was actually wrong.
description.output: A short finished announcement video whose script and final render each passed a real human check.

activities.label: Read the feature description and past approved taste
Settle the script and the visual strategy together
Get the script approved before anything is spent
Produce the voiceover
Compose the final render
Present the render for the second decision

outcomes.statement: A feature description becomes a finished announcement video, with the script and the final render each getting a real human check before moving on.
success_criteria: The script is approved before voiceover synthesis spends anything
A rejection routes back to the specific stage it affects, not a full restart

recipes.guidance: Turn a feature description into a short announcement video: work out the script and visual strategy, get them approved, then produce the voiceover and compose the render for a second decision. Keep rework scoped; if only the voiceover is wrong, redo the voiceover rather than the whole pipeline. Treat the approval gates as real checkpoints rather than formalities, and when input is too thin to work from, ask before drafting.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The work becomes worth doing when a feature has shipped without an announcement. Nothing in the source evidences a release event this recipe can listen to, and a calendar would produce videos for weeks with nothing to announce.

personalization_needs: What the adopter's product sounds like when it announces something, since tone is the dimension rejections cluster on and it cannot be read from the feature description
Who the announcement is for, because the same feature is pitched differently to existing users and to prospects
Where the finished video is going, since a channel's length and aspect ratio constraints decide the script before the script is written

input_schema.name: duration

input_schema.name: style
input_schema.description: Default visual style. The agent refines this from review feedback over time.

recipes.title: Source artifact repurposing for channels

description.need: Something published once reaches only the audience of the place it was published, and reformatting it by hand for every other channel is the work that quietly stops getting done.
description.input: One published artifact in whatever form it exists, a video, an article, a transcript or pasted text, plus the written voice description for each channel in scope.
description.core_action: Produce what each channel actually needs from the source, as a rewrite grounded in that channel's own voice description rather than the same text reformatted.
description.output: One draft per channel in scope, each respecting that channel's constraints and voice, each waiting on its own separate approval.

activities.label: Resolve the source artifact into text worth working from
Read the voice description for each channel in scope
Decide what each channel actually wants from this source
Write a channel specific draft rather than an excerpt
Present each draft for its own separate approval

outcomes.statement: Something published once is present wherever its audience is, in a form that fits each place.
success_criteria: Each draft respects its channel's own constraints and voice rather than being the same text reformatted
Nothing is published without an explicit approval for that specific channel
A channel whose voice description is missing is held back and named, rather than drafted generically

recipes.guidance: Take a published piece and produce what each channel needs from it. A channel variant is a rewrite, not an excerpt, and it is grounded in that channel's own written voice rather than a generic house style. Approval is per channel, so one being turned down does not hold the others. When a draft cannot meet a channel's hard constraint, show the constraint failure alongside the draft rather than silently truncating it.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. The work begins when a source artifact is published; there is nothing to repurpose before that and no reason to look on a clock.

personalization_needs: Which channels are in scope, since drafting for a channel with no account is waste
Where source artifacts come from and whether their arrival should trigger this at all, because a channel feed and a manual paste are different levels of automation
What the adopter considers a source worth repurposing, since not everything published deserves a fan out

input_schema.name: target_platforms

I kept them as two recipes because the lane requires all 27 ids present, and flagged the merge for the Director; if merged, this recipe's activities lead and the publishing recipe's activities finish the sequence, which stays linear and branch free. recipes.title: Approved draft channel publishing

description.need: Approved work sits unpublished, and the person who approved it has no way to tell whether their decision reached the world.
description.input: A draft that has been approved for one named channel, plus the adopter's preference for whether approved work goes live now or joins a queue.
description.core_action: Carry the approved draft through to actually being live or scheduled on the channel it was approved for, and report what happened with a link or a time.
description.output: The piece is live or queued on its channel, and the approval is confirmed with the artifact link or the scheduled time rather than disappearing.

activities.label: Read the approval and the channel it names
Match the destination to that channel's own posting shape
Publish or queue the piece
Confirm with the artifact link or the scheduled time

outcomes.statement: An approved draft either goes live or scheduled, or its failure is surfaced with what to do about it.
success_criteria: The destination matches the channel the draft was approved for, rather than one dispatch path applied to everything
A confirmation carrying the published link or the scheduled time always follows
A destination failure leaves the draft intact and says what to do about it, rather than dropping it or retrying against a different channel

recipes.guidance: React to an approval by getting the draft where it was approved to go, matching the destination to the channel rather than applying one dispatch path to everything. Treat publication as part of the job rather than a separate step. Always confirm what happened and where, so an approval does not feel like it disappeared. When a destination fails, keep the draft and say what to do about it; never quietly reroute to another channel.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. An approval is a real external event and the only honest starting point; publishing before it would defeat the gate and polling for it would add latency for nothing.

personalization_needs: Which channels the adopter actually posts to, since a destination with no account is a failure waiting for the first approval
Whether approved work publishes immediately or goes into a queue, which is a control preference rather than a configuration value
Who should be told when a publish fails, because the failure is only useful if it reaches the person who approved the draft

recipes.title: Per channel writing voice profiling

description.need: Drafts written without a written description of how this person sounds read like nobody, and the same correction gets made on every draft forever because nothing records it.
description.input: A handful of the person's own best posts on one channel, and the corrections that have accumulated on drafts for that channel.
description.core_action: Derive from real examples how they open, how long their sentences run, what words they never use and how they close, and write it down concretely enough that a draft can be checked against it.
description.output: One written voice description per channel, derived from real work rather than adjectives, revised when corrections start clustering rather than repeated.

activities.label: Gather the person's own best posts for one channel
Extract hooks, sentence rhythm, vocabulary and closing shape
Write the description concretely enough to check a draft against
Put it in front of the person before drafts are made from it

outcomes.statement: Drafts read as though the person wrote them, and read differently on each channel because each channel is different.
success_criteria: Each channel has a written description of its voice, derived from real examples rather than adjectives
A change to one channel's voice does not leak into another's
Repeated corrections on the same dimension change the description rather than being corrected again

recipes.guidance: Own the written description of how this person sounds on each channel: how they open, how long their sentences run, what words they never use, how they close. Derive it from their actual best work. When drafts keep getting corrected the same way, the description is wrong and should be revised rather than the correction repeated. Never generalise one channel's voice onto another, and say when the sample was too thin to be confident.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when corrections on a channel start clustering on one dimension, when a new channel is added, or when the person's own recent work has moved away from the description.

personalization_needs: Real examples of the person's own best posts per channel, which is the only usable input here and cannot be substituted with a style label
Which channels matter, since building a voice for a channel nobody posts to is waste
What the person considers off voice, which is often easier for them to state than what is on voice

input_schema.name: target_platform
input_schema.description: Which platform's voice doc to build. Run once per platform; re-runnable per platform independently.

input_schema.name: sample_posts
input_schema.description: 3-5 of your best posts on the target platform, separated by `---`. Either pasted directly or as a list of URLs the agent fetches.

recipes.review_notes: The designed responsibility declares no connectors and neither does v2, which survives review: sample posts arrive pasted, and the URL path degrades to a paste. The single largest change from v2 is the trigger. v2 called this a build time one shot that is 're-runnable when your voice evolves'; the designed responsibility makes revision the normal case and names the signal for it, corrections clustering on one dimension. That is a better recipe and I followed it. The v2 storage path inside design_context is an installation detail and is gone.

recipes.title: Newsletter issue curation and delivery

description.need: A newsletter assembled from whatever the feeds produced is a link dump, and subscribers stop opening it long before anyone notices the sources went stale.
description.input: The sources the adopter follows, the record of what past issues already covered, and the editorial corrections reviewers have made before.
description.core_action: Judge which items are actually worth a subscriber's attention, group what belongs together, and write real commentary saying why each matters rather than restating the headline.
description.output: One edited issue that repeats nothing from a past issue, passes a human read, and reaches the subscriber list, with any source that has stopped working named.

activities.label: Pull from the followed sources and note which failed
Drop what past issues already covered
Judge what is genuinely worth including and what is not
Group into sections and write the editorial commentary
Put the assembled issue in front of a human before it sends
Deliver to the subscriber list

outcomes.statement: Each issue is genuinely curated and deduplicated against past issues, and reads as edited content rather than a raw feed dump, before it reaches subscribers.
success_criteria: Articles are scored and selected, not included wholesale
Every issue passes human review before send
No article repeats one already covered in a past issue

outcomes.statement: A source that has stopped working is noticed rather than silently producing nothing.
success_criteria: A source failing repeatedly is named in the issue rather than quietly contributing zero items
A thin period ships a short issue rather than padding to a target count

recipes.guidance: Pull from the followed sources and keep only what would actually change something for a reader; most published items are noise and the accountability is the ratio, not the volume. Deduplicate rigorously against past issues. Write commentary that says why an item matters in terms of the reader's work, because an item filed without that is a link nobody opens. Nothing reaches the subscriber list without a human read first.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The designed ingest responsibilities pace to how fast each source actually publishes, which differs per source. An issue is worth sending when there is enough worth reading, and the v2 weekly cron was a subscriber expectation the adopter sets on the charter rather than an obligation on the craft.

personalization_needs: Which sources the adopter follows and which they gave up on, since a stale source list is worse than none
What the adopter's readers are watching for, because relevance here is entirely a function of what they are working on
Who the subscriber list is and how it is held, since delivery is the one step that cannot be undone
The editorial voice the commentary should carry, which reviewers will otherwise correct issue after issue
dependencies: a subscriber list the chosen email connector is able to send to

input_schema.name: max_articles_per_issue
input_schema.description: Max articles per issue. Fewer allowed if quality candidates are scarce.

input_schema.name: source_scan_depth
input_schema.description: Days back to scan. High-priority sources exempt from the age filter.

input_schema.name: editorial_tone
input_schema.description: Writing voice for headlines, commentary, and section intros.

examples.title: Firecrawl as the source reader
examples.notes: Catalogued as web_scraping and research. Covers both the feed case and the page case the designed responsibilities separate; a page that only changed its markup is not a new item, which is the judgment the connector cannot make for you.

examples.title: Resend or SendGrid as the delivery connector
examples.notes: Catalogued as email, alongside sendgrid, gmail, microsoft-outlook and hubspot. A list send and a personal mail send are different products; adoption should check that the chosen connector actually holds the subscriber list rather than assuming any email connector will do.

The three superseding Harvester responsibilities (Feed ingest, Page and site ingest, Inbox ingest) are all domain product_project and all end at making an item visible in a backlog; none of them curates, writes, assembles or sends a newsletter. Applied as authoritative they would delete the recipe rather than reshape it. I took from them what genuinely governs the first half (relevance over volume, dedupe across sources, a failing source is a reportable fact, say why an item matters) and kept the consolidation verdict's outcome for the second half, which nothing in the designed corpus covers. The second outcome here is assembled from Feed ingest's third success criterion. Inbox ingest's email trigger is not carried: an inbound mail source is a different intake and folding it in would put a branch in the activities.
recipes.research_notes: Confirmed email membership: gmail, resend, sendgrid, microsoft-outlook, hubspot and the google workspace template, six connectors. None of them declares a subscriber list resource in the catalog, which is why the list is stated as a dependency rather than assumed to come with the connector. web_scraping members are apify, bright-data and firecrawl.

recipes.title: Conversion experiment significance watch

description.need: An experiment called early is worse than no experiment, because the wrong variant then ships with the authority of a measurement behind it.
description.input: The ledger of in flight experiments with their start dates, per arm counts and target metric, and the guardrails the adopter set for what earns a verdict.
description.core_action: Decide for each experiment whether it has actually earned a verdict yet, watching for signs the measurement itself is broken, and propose what to do rather than doing it.
description.output: Each in flight experiment carries a current, defensible classification, and every promote, revert or archive sits as a proposal a person can accept or refuse.

activities.label: Read the current state of every in flight experiment
Check each against sample size and duration before computing anything
Classify what has earned a verdict and what is still running
Flag results the arithmetic itself argues against
Put each promote, revert or archive up as a proposal

outcomes.statement: No experiment is called a winner or loser before it has actually earned that call statistically.
success_criteria: An experiment below the configured sample size or minimum duration is left running, never classified early.
A split imbalance or a mathematically inconsistent result, such as a negative lift reading as a win, is flagged as suspicious rather than acted on.

outcomes.statement: Nobody's live traffic changes without a person having approved it.
success_criteria: Every promote, revert or archive action sits in review before the backend is called; refusals are recorded as learning rather than retried silently.

recipes.guidance: Own knowing the true state of every in flight experiment and proposing what to do about it, never quietly acting on the site yourself. Apply the sample size and duration guardrails before calling a winner, and watch for signs the maths itself is broken, an imbalanced split or a statistically winning result with negative lift. Route every promote, revert or archive to the person running the program before it touches production.

recommended_trigger.rationale: An experiment reaches significance on its own traffic, not on a calendar. Look when enough new data has accumulated to plausibly change a verdict, and less often once every experiment is well below its guardrails. The v2 Monday cron was a reporting habit shared across three capabilities.

personalization_needs: What the adopter counts as conversion here, since the whole verdict is computed against one metric and the wrong one produces confident nonsense
How much traffic the site actually gets, because a sample size guardrail set without it either never fires or never holds
Which changes the seat may propose and how consequential a live traffic change is considered here, which sets how cautious the classification should be
dependencies: an experimentation backend able to split traffic and report per arm counts

input_schema.name: min_sample_size
input_schema.description: Minimum visitors per arm before significance is computed. Lower = faster but noisier.

input_schema.name: min_duration_days
input_schema.description: Minimum experiment duration before a winner can be called, regardless of sample size.

input_schema.name: significance_threshold
input_schema.description: p-value threshold for the two-proportion z-test. 0.05 is the scientific default.

examples.title: Humbalytics as the experimentation backend
examples.notes: Its catalog summary is web analytics with built in A/B experimentation that rewrites page content without redeploying code. It is the one connector in the catalog that supplies both halves this recipe needs, the per arm counts and the deployment surface.

examples.title: PostHog as the experimentation backend
examples.notes: Catalogued as analytics and monitoring; its summary names feature flags and A/B testing. A projects resource is declared, so adoption can pick which project the experiments live in.

recipes.review_notes: Not superseded, so outcomes and guidance are the consolidation verdict's, lightly reworded to remove em dashes. The v2 recipe referred to an unnamed 'experimentation backend'; research showed the analytics category genuinely contains connectors that do this, so the type is honest and the dependency line names the capability rather than a vendor. The RUNNING, WINNER, LOSER, INCONCLUSIVE vocabulary is installation detail and did not survive into the description; the judgment that an unearned verdict is a defect did.
recipes.research_notes: Read humbalytics.json and posthog.json. humbalytics summary: 'Humbalytics web analytics with built-in A/B experimentation, traffic attribution, heat maps, and scroll-depth tracking. Runs experiments that dynamically rewrite page content without redeploying code.' posthog summary: 'PostHog product analytics, feature flags, session replay, and A/B testing', declaring a projects resource. There is no experimentation category in the catalog, so analytics is the correct and only legal type; recorded as a lane finding since it also resolves to read only connectors like mixpanel that cannot deploy a variant.

recipes.title: Conversion variant hypothesis proposals

description.need: Pages underperform quietly, and the ideas offered for them are usually generic best practice that would apply to any site and therefore explains nothing about this one.
description.input: Per page conversion rates against their own rolling baselines, the pages the adopter has allowed to be experimented on, and the record of which kinds of change have been accepted or refused before.
description.core_action: Rank pages by how far below their own baseline they sit and write a small number of hypotheses specific to what is actually underperforming on each, each naming what it expects to move.
description.output: A short set of testable proposals, each citing the page's specific gap and its expected effect, waiting on a person to choose which run.

activities.label: Read per page conversion against each page's own baseline
Rank pages by how far below baseline they sit
Set aside pages out of scope and change categories already refused
Write hypotheses specific to each page's actual gap
Present them for a person to choose from

outcomes.statement: Every underperforming page gets a small set of testable hypotheses grounded in its actual numbers, not generic advice.
success_criteria: Each proposal names the page's specific conversion gap against baseline
Each proposal states expected lift and the metric it targets
No page gets more than the configured cap of hypotheses per run

outcomes.statement: No experiment reaches the live site without a human choosing to run it.
success_criteria: Every proposal sits in human review before deployment
Only approved proposals reach the experimentation backend

recipes.guidance: Prioritise pages by how far below baseline they sit, and keep hypotheses specific to what is actually underperforming rather than reusable boilerplate. State expected lift honestly, including when it is a rough estimate. Never propose against a page the adopter placed out of bounds. Nothing here should ever deploy without a person choosing to; the job ends at a proposal a reviewer can accept or refuse with confidence.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Proposals are worth writing when the performance reading has moved enough to argue for something new, and when the existing experiments are not already saturating the pages in scope. A weekly clock produces proposals into a full queue.

personalization_needs: Which pages may be experimented on at all, since checkout and legal pages are usually out of bounds and the cost of getting that wrong is not recoverable
What the adopter is trying to move on each page, because the same copy change is an improvement against one metric and a regression against another
Which kinds of change the adopter has already refused, so the same category is not proposed a fourth time
dependencies: an experimentation backend able to split traffic and report per arm counts

input_schema.name: max_new_variants_per_run
input_schema.description: Cap on new variant proposals per run to avoid interaction effects on the same page.

input_schema.name: target_pages
input_schema.description: Comma-separated URL paths allowed for experimentation (e.g. `/, /pricing, /features`). Pages NOT in this list are never touched. Legal/checkout pages should be excluded.

examples.title: Humbalytics as the analytics and experimentation source
examples.notes: Supplies both the per page conversion reading this recipe proposes from and the deployment surface an accepted proposal lands on, which is why one connector_type covers the whole loop here.

examples.title: A read only analytics connector
examples.notes: Catalogued as analytics only. It can supply the underperformance reading but cannot deploy an accepted variant, so an adoption resolving analytics to it needs a second binding for the deployment half or the recipe stops at the proposal.

recipes.review_notes: Not superseded; outcomes and guidance from the consolidation verdict. The v2 15 percent below baseline threshold is a knob and left the description, but the judgment behind it, rank against each page's own baseline rather than a fixed target, is in the activities and the guidance. The excluded pages rule was in v2 error handling only; promoted into guidance and a personalization need because it is the one irreversible mistake this recipe can make.
recipes.research_notes: Same catalog reading as the significance watch. Confirmed the analytics category has eight members: duckdb, formbricks, humbalytics, metabase, mixpanel, posthog, redash, twilio-segment. Only humbalytics and posthog evidence any experimentation capability, so the type is broad relative to what this recipe needs; recorded in an example note rather than narrowed by invention.

recipes.title: Conversion experiment program digest

description.need: An optimisation program that only communicates when something wins leaves its owner unable to tell a quiet period from a stalled one.
description.input: The current state of every experiment, the verdicts reached since the last digest, the proposals waiting, and what was archived without reaching significance.
description.core_action: Compose one honest account of where the whole program stands, including the uncertainty, rather than reporting only the parts that look like progress.
description.output: One briefing covering what is running, what came back, what is proposed and what was archived, delivered whether or not the period was eventful.

activities.label: Gather the program's current state and everything decided since the last look
Judge how much confidence each result actually carries
Compose the account at the depth the reader asked for
Deliver it whether or not the period was eventful

outcomes.statement: Whoever owns conversion optimisation has a complete view of every experiment, win and proposal, whether or not anything got reviewed.
success_criteria: The briefing goes out even when there is nothing significant to report
In flight experiments, results, new proposals and inconclusive archives are all represented
An early or weakly supported result is presented with its uncertainty rather than as a finding

recipes.guidance: Compose the program's status in one place: what is running, what came back significant, what is proposed next, and what got archived as inconclusive. Deliver it regardless of how eventful the period was, because visibility is the job rather than news. Keep the summary honest about uncertainty rather than overselling early results, and when the account cannot be assembled, say so plainly instead of shipping a confident empty one.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The digest is worth composing when the program has moved, and its rhythm is a delivery preference the adopter sets on the charter. The v2 Monday cron was shared across three capabilities that no longer need to share a clock.

personalization_needs: Who reads this and what decision they make from it, because an executive summary and a working document are different artifacts
How the adopter wants to be told, since a briefing that arrives where they do not look is not visibility
What quiet looks like for this program, so that an uneventful period reads as reassurance rather than as a broken watch

input_schema.name: report_depth
input_schema.description: Executive: top-line only. Standard: tables + per-experiment detail. Deep: + per-page variant history.

recipes.review_notes: Retitled away from 'Combined CRO Report', which named an internal composition rather than an area and an activity. v2 declared no connectors and the delivery channel was the app's own message surface, which is not a connector; connector_types stays empty rather than inventing messaging. This is one of three siblings from the same template that shared a single cron; with all three now self_paced, the sharing is gone and the Director should note that the digest is the only one of the three whose rhythm the adopter genuinely has an opinion about.
recipes.research_notes: No connector research applied. Confirmed against the catalog that the in app message surface used by v2 has no connector entry, so declaring messaging or notifications here would have been an invented dependency.

recipes.title: Website conversion gap audit

description.need: A site can look finished and still lose every visitor at the same place, and a list of everything imperfect tells the owner nothing about which gap is costing them.
description.input: The properties the operator sells from, what each page was supposed to achieve, the score history of previous passes, and the findings already declined.
description.core_action: Judge each category by what the gap costs in visitors or ranking position rather than in taste, comparing the site against what it itself scored last time.
description.output: A prioritised set of open findings, each with a severity that means the same thing it did on the first pass, a raised date and a decision, with declined ones still visible as declined.

activities.label: Read the target property and the pages that carry the conversion
Score each category against what it costs in visitors or position
Compare against this site's own previous scores rather than a benchmark
Rank open findings by cost and carry forward what was declined
Deliver the findings for a decision on each

outcomes.statement: The properties the operator sells from carry no known, unaddressed gap that costs a visitor or a ranking position.
success_criteria: Every open finding has a severity, a decision from the operator, and the date it was first raised
A finding that was accepted and fixed disappears from the next pass instead of being raised again
Movement in a category can be traced to a specific change that was made

outcomes.statement: Severity means the same thing on the hundredth audit as it did on the first.
success_criteria: A critical finding always names what it costs in visitors or position, not in taste
Findings the operator declined stay visible as declined rather than being silently re-raised or dropped

recipes.guidance: Own whether the site converts and ranks, not whether it looks good. Judge each category by what it costs in visitors or position, and keep severity honest so that critical still means critical after a hundred passes. Compare the site against what it itself scored last time rather than a generic benchmark. Escalate anything that needs a product or content decision instead of guessing at intent, and treat a site that is down or blocking you as a finding rather than a failed run.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when the site has changed since the last look, when a finding raised earlier should now be verifiably fixed, or when a category has gone long enough unexamined that its score is stale.

personalization_needs: Which properties count, and what winning looks like on each of them, whether signups, traffic or position on named queries, because severity is meaningless until the persona knows what the page was supposed to achieve
Which findings the operator has already decided not to act on, since without this the same declined gap returns every pass and the report loses credibility

How much of the site is rendered on the server, because structural analysis of a client rendered page misses forms and proof that exist at runtime and the audit must state that limit rather than score them zero

input_schema.name: target_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the website to audit (e.g. https://example-hvac.com).

input_schema.name: business_type
input_schema.description: Type of local service business. Drives industry-specific benchmarks.

input_schema.name: audit_depth
input_schema.description: Quick = homepage only. Standard = homepage + key subpages. Deep = all discoverable pages.

input_schema.name: min_severity
input_schema.description: Only include findings at or above this severity level.

recipes.review_notes: A real departure from v2, taken deliberately because the designed responsibility is a better recipe. v2 audited a client's site for a local service business and prioritised by revenue impact using industry benchmarks; the designed responsibility audits the operator's own properties and explicitly compares against the site's own previous scores rather than a benchmark. I followed the designed responsibility for outcomes, guidance, trigger and personalization. The consequence is that the business_type input schema, carried verbatim as the spec requires, now describes a benchmark set the guidance no longer leans on. The Director should decide whether that knob survives the transform.

Considered adding web_scraping for the bot protection case that v2 error handling names, and declined, because neither source evidences a scraping connector and adding one would promise a capability the recipe does not have.

recipes.title: Competitor conversion and positioning comparison

description.need: A snapshot of where competitors stand today says nothing about which direction anyone is moving, and a comparison scored on a different yardstick than the home site means nothing at all.
description.input: The named competitors that actually compete for the same decision, the ledger of what each has claimed before with first seen dates, and the same scoring categories used on the operator's own property.
description.core_action: Read what has changed since the last look, a feature that appeared, pricing that moved, a claim withdrawn, and score it on the identical categories so the comparison is honest.
description.output: A comparison reporting movement rather than only current state, saying plainly where a competitor is simply better and which competitors have stopped moving.

activities.label: Read each named competitor's current public position
Establish what moved since the last look and when it first appeared
Score on the identical categories used on the home property
Report the movement, including where a competitor is simply better

outcomes.statement: The operator knows what competitors shipped since the last look and how his own position moved against them.
success_criteria: Every competitor claim carries a first seen date so movement is visible rather than implied
A comparison reports what changed since the previous comparison, not only current state
A competitor that has stopped moving is reported as such rather than quietly dropped
A competitor that could not be reached is named as unreached, never silently omitted

recipes.guidance: Track competitors as a moving picture rather than a snapshot. What matters is the delta since the last look: a feature that appeared, pricing that moved, a claim that was withdrawn. Score them on the same categories used on the operator's own property so the comparison is honest. Say plainly where a competitor is simply better, and never pad a comparison to make the home side look good.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Competitors ship on their own schedule, so watch for evidence that something moved, a changed page, a release note, a pricing change, and look then.

personalization_needs: Which competitors actually compete for the same decision, and why the operator picked them, because a list chosen by market category tracks the wrong companies and produces confident irrelevance
Which features or claims the operator considers his ground to defend, since movement matters only relative to what he is trying to win and everything else is trivia
How the operator wants a competitor who is genuinely ahead described, because a comparison nobody trusts to say so is not read twice

input_schema.name: competitor_urls
input_schema.description: Comma-separated competitor URLs for side-by-side comparison.

recipes.review_notes: The designed responsibility is substantially wider than v2 and I followed it. v2 was a comparison section appended to an audit run, alive only when competitor URLs were configured; the designed responsibility owns a standing competitor ledger with first seen dates and reports movement rather than state. That turns a dependent add on into a recipe that stands alone, which is why it now has its own trigger rather than running alongside the audit. The unreachable competitor criterion is carried from the v2 error handling because it is a real honesty rule the designed responsibility does not state.
recipes.research_notes: No connectors are declared by either source and none is needed; reading a competitor's public pages is an agent capability. Checked whether the research category would fit and declined: its members are academic and market data sources (arxiv, pubmed, semantic-scholar, news_api, alpha-vantage, kalshi) plus scraping connectors, none of which this recipe is evidenced to require.

recipes.title: Community discussion trend digest

description.need: The communities where a product's users talk about it move faster than anyone can read, and a digest that pads itself to look consistent teaches its readers to skip it.
description.input: The communities the adopter follows, the index of posts already covered, and the corrections reviewers have made to past digests.
description.core_action: Cluster genuinely new discussion into the few themes that actually ran, label the sentiment honestly, and ship fewer themes on a quiet day rather than stretching thin material.
description.output: A short themed digest of what those communities actually discussed, delivered where the team reads, saying plainly when there was nothing.

activities.label: Pull recent activity from the followed communities
Drop what previous digests already covered
Cluster the remainder into the themes that genuinely ran
Label sentiment and decide what is worth a reader's attention
Deliver the digest, or say plainly that there was nothing

outcomes.statement: The digest reflects what the followed communities actually discussed in the period, never padded to look busier than it was.
success_criteria: The digest ships fewer clusters on a quiet day rather than stretching thin content to hit the configured maximum
A period with no new discussion still ships a one line note rather than going silent

recipes.guidance: Turn raw community activity into themed clusters with sentiment a team can actually use, never manufacturing volume to look consistent. Deduplicate against what has already been covered so themes reflect genuinely new discussion, and respect the content boundaries the team set. recipes.title: Content source health tracking

description.need: A source that has quietly stopped yielding anything looks identical to a quiet one, so dead entries stay on a follow list forever and spend budget every pass.
description.input: The outcome of each fetch against each followed source, and the record of when each last produced something usable.
description.core_action: Distinguish a source that is quiet from a source that is broken by requiring a clear run of failures before saying anything, then recommend removal rather than continuing to poll.
description.output: Each followed source carries a current health state, and a source that has been failing long enough is named for removal in the next digest.

activities.label: Record the outcome of each fetch against each source
Decide whether the pattern is quiet or broken
Raise a source whose failures have become a clear pattern
Carry a removal recommendation into the next digest

outcomes.statement: A source that has stopped yielding usable content long enough to be dead weight gets flagged for removal instead of silently wasting fetch budget forever.
success_criteria: A source failing repeatedly enough to be a pattern raises a health signal and a removal recommendation in the next digest
A single failure or a genuinely quiet period does not raise anything

recipes.guidance: Track whether each followed source is still worth fetching, as a background responsibility to the digest rather than a job of its own. Record outcomes per source and only call a source unhealthy once the pattern is clear, then recommend removal rather than silently continuing to poll something dead. A corrupted health record is safe to start again from empty; the history is useful but not critical.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The only thing this recipe reacts to is a fetch outcome, which is a real observable event produced by whichever recipe is doing the fetching. There is nothing to look at between fetches and nothing a clock would add.

personalization_needs: How many failures the adopter considers a pattern rather than an outage, because being too eager here removes a source that was merely down for an afternoon
Who decides whether a flagged source is actually removed, since this recipe recommends and does not prune
Which sources the adopter considers load bearing, because a high value source failing deserves an interruption while a marginal one deserves a line in a digest

description.core_action: Find the specific forums, communities, newsletters and directories where this product's actual users already gather, offering few and specific rather than many and plausible.

Look for where this product's users already gather
Judge each candidate on fit rather than audience size
Present a small set for a good or bad decision on each

success_criteria: Each suggested surface is justified by what the product does, not by generic popularity
Surfaces already tried are not suggested again
Surfaces that turned out to be noise stop appearing, and the categories they belong to are suppressed

recipes.guidance: Find the forums, communities, newsletters and directories where this product's actual users already are. Ground the search in what the product genuinely does, read from its own materials, because the failure mode here is generic suggestions that fit any product. Offer few and specific rather than many and plausible. Take the tagging of good and bad seriously; a category rejected twice should not come back a third time.

Whether the adopter wants suggestions only, or wants drafted approaches too

recipes.title: Web content performance review

description.need: Movement in a product's own numbers goes unnoticed until it is too late to act on, and a table of metrics with no interpretation is not a read on anything.
description.input: The product's own metrics for the period, the rolling baseline each page is normally measured against, and the anomalies already raised and still open.
description.core_action: Judge each move against what this product normally does rather than a fixed threshold, allowing a wider band for low volume pages, and end in a proposal or an explicit nothing worth doing.
description.output: A grounded read on what moved and why it matters, with each anomaly stated against the baseline it deviated from, and a next step or a clear statement that there is none.

activities.label: Read the period's metrics and how complete they are
Compare each move against that page's own rolling baseline
Rank what is worth attention and set aside routine variance
Explain what the movement means rather than restating it
Deliver the read ending in a proposal or an explicit nothing

outcomes.statement: Movement in the product's numbers is noticed while it can still be acted on, and explained rather than only reported.
success_criteria: A move is stated against the baseline it deviated from
A quiet period produces no report and no doubt that the watch is running
An anomaly already raised is not raised again on the next look

outcomes.statement: Numbers turn into a next step.
success_criteria: Each analysis ends in a proposal or an explicit nothing worth doing
A proposal names what it expects to change so it can be measured later

recipes.guidance: Own what the numbers mean for what to do next, not the production of a report. A move only matters against what this product normally does, and low volume pages need a wider band before anything is called an anomaly. Anything worth acting on becomes a proposal, and anything not worth acting on stays quiet. Say clearly when the data itself is incomplete rather than reporting through the gap.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Look when the data plausibly moved: enough new data to judge, a change that shipped and should now be visible, or an open anomaly still unexplained. A partial period is extended rather than rescanned.

personalization_needs: Which database holds these metrics and what a normal period looks like there, because anomaly detection without a learned normal is a threshold guess dressed up as analysis
What the operator counts as success for this content, since the same traffic drop is a problem on one page and irrelevant on another
Which pages carry enough traffic to be judged at all, so that low volume noise does not dominate the read

recipes.title: Content metrics anomaly check

description.need: Waiting for the end of a period to discover something moved wastes the half of the period in which it could still have been acted on.
description.input: Partial period metrics, the trajectory the baseline says the period should be on by this point, and the anomalies already raised.
description.core_action: Compare where the numbers actually are against where the baseline says they should be by now, and say nothing at all when they are tracking normally.
description.output: Silence when the period is normal, and a named deviation with its magnitude when it is not.

activities.label: Read the period so far
Derive where the baseline says the period should be by now
Decide whether the gap is a deviation or routine variance
Raise only what is worth acting on, and stay silent otherwise

outcomes.statement: The team only hears from this check when something has actually moved off the expected trajectory.
success_criteria: Partial period metrics are compared against a baseline derived expectation, not a raw threshold
No alert fires when the period is tracking normally
An anomaly already raised is not raised again on the next look

recipes.guidance: Check whether metrics are tracking where the baseline says they should be, and say nothing when they are. The value here is restraint: only surface a deviation worth acting on, not routine variance. Keep the baseline itself trustworthy so that silence actually means normal, and treat a data source that is unavailable as a reason to stay quiet rather than a reason to raise noise.

recipes.title: Paid and organic channel performance scan

description.need: Paid and organic performance sit in separate dashboards, so nobody reads them together and the findings that only exist between them are never found.

description.core_action: Read both channels against what is normal for this account rather than against last period alone, and report degradation honestly when one source is unavailable.
description.output: One honest read on whether performance is improving, stable or declining, at the depth asked for, that the rest of the marketing work can build on.

Read the organic side for the same period
Compare both against their own rolling baselines
Flag what moved beyond normal variation
Report the read, naming any source that was unavailable

outcomes.statement: Paid and organic performance are read together against a rolling baseline, so a normal fluctuation is distinguishable from a real change.
success_criteria: Movements are reported against a rolling baseline rather than against the previous period alone
If one platform is unavailable, the other channel's read still happens and the outage is named rather than hidden by an empty report
The read stops at observation; it does not propose changes itself

recipes.guidance: Read paid and organic together, because the interesting findings live between them. Report movement against what is normal for this account rather than against last period alone. This responsibility observes and reports; the changes it argues for belong to whoever proposes them. When one side is unavailable, say so and process the other rather than shipping a report that looks complete and is not.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. Act when enough has changed to be worth reading, which for most accounts is slower than weekly and for a live campaign is faster. The v2 Monday cron was shared across three sibling capabilities rather than earned by any of them.

personalization_needs: What the adopter is trying to move, because a signup goal and a revenue goal make opposite readings of the same numbers
What counts as a meaningful amount of money here, which sets the floor for what is worth reporting at all
How fast this account actually moves, since the pacing of the read is the whole difference between a useful signal and constant noise

recipes.title: Paid and organic keyword cannibalization watch

description.need: Money is spent bidding on terms the site already wins organically, and because the two numbers live in different systems nobody ever puts them side by side.
description.input: The keywords currently being paid for with their spend, and the organic ranking positions for those same keywords.
description.core_action: Cross reference the two and judge where the paid spend is buying traffic that was already arriving, putting a number on what that is costing.
description.output: Each overlapping keyword flagged with the money it is plausibly wasting, and the boundary cases sent for a person to judge rather than asserted.

activities.label: Read which keywords are being paid for and what they cost
Read the organic position for those same keywords
Judge where paid spend is buying traffic already arriving
Put a number on what each overlap is costing
Surface the clear cases and route the boundary ones for judgment

outcomes.statement: Spend on terms that already win organically is identified with the amount it is costing.
success_criteria: Every flagged keyword includes the calculated savings estimate, not just a flag
When organic rank sits exactly at the boundary or the paid and organic paths cannot be cleanly separated, the finding routes to a person instead of being asserted as certain
Nothing is flagged when only one of the two sides has data, since there is nothing to conclude from one side alone

Treat boundary cases, a rank sitting exactly at the cutoff or attribution that cannot be cleanly separated, as judgment calls for a person rather than certainties to assert. The number is the point: a flag without it cannot be acted on.

How the adopter separates paid from organic conversion, because the estimate is only as honest as that separation

Nothing enters the backlog without a person accepting it

recipes.review_notes: Three responsibilities supersede this recipe and only one governs it. 'Leads arriving through a form' is authoritative and supplies the outcome, the trigger and the personalization needs. 'Leads arriving by mail' is a different intake with a different door and belongs to a recipe this lane does not contain. 'Nobody who reached out is dropped' is a self paced reconciliation responsibility, and it is the honest home for the v2 polling safety net; I did not fold it in, because a recipe that both listens for an event and sweeps for missed ones has a branch in it, which the spec forbids. The result is that retiring the polling safety net leaves a real gap in the surviving corpus, recorded as a lane finding. Departure from the designed responsibility: it declares four connectors covering the whole cluster (forms, crm, email, messaging); this recipe declares only the two it actually touches.
recipes.research_notes: Read tally.json (forms), formbricks.json (forms, analytics) and airtable.json. Confirmed the crm category has four members: attio, hubspot, monday and pipedrive. Airtable is not among them despite being the store the v2 recipe actually wrote to, which is a genuine adoption trap worth the Director's attention. Also confirmed forms has only two members, so a lead pipeline whose form vendor is neither has no legal binding for this type.

recipes.title: Lead welcome email drafting

description.need: One template sent to everyone reads as a template to everyone, and the person who wrote three sentences about their problem learns immediately that nobody read them.
description.input: A newly judged lead with the reasoning behind that judgment, what they actually wrote, and the adopter's rule for which cases a person should see before anything sends.
description.core_action: Match the reply to how ready this person actually is, drawing on what they wrote rather than substituting a name into a template.
description.output: A first reply that reflects the person who sent it, sent or held for approval according to the boundary the adopter set.

activities.label: Read the lead, what they wrote, and how promising they were judged
Decide how direct the reply should be for this person
Draft a reply grounded in what they actually said
Hold for approval where the adopter's boundary says to
Send, and record that it went

outcomes.statement: A new lead's first reply reflects what they actually wrote and how ready they are, rather than a single template with a name substituted.
success_criteria: A low intent enquiry gets something useful and low pressure; a high intent one gets a direct next step
The reply draws on the content of their submission, not only on their tier
No reply claims something about the product that is not true

outcomes.statement: The cases the adopter wants to see before they go out do not go out without being seen.
success_criteria: Replies in the gated set wait for a person, and the rest do not wait for no reason
A reply that could not be sent is queued and named rather than silently dropped

recipes.guidance: Draft and send a first reply tuned to how ready the lead actually is: something useful and low pressure for an early enquiry, a direct next step for a serious one. The judgment is in the reply, so someone who wrote three sentences about their problem should not get what someone who typed a name gets. Respect the approval boundary the adopter drew, and never claim something about the product that is not true.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Taken from the designed responsibility. The reply is owed the moment a lead is captured, and its value decays quickly; a clock would send it after the moment it was worth having.

personalization_needs: Whether replies send automatically or wait for approval, and whether that differs by how promising the lead is, which is a trust boundary rather than a setting
What is actually true about the product and what may be offered, since this recipe writes on the adopter's behalf to someone they have never met
Who a serious lead should be handed to and how they should be named in the reply, because a personal note from nobody in particular is worse than an honest general one
